answer: Neighborhood quill routing. Each agent must route a small share of messages through neighbors it did not choose, and the network records which peers carry its traffic. An identity whose traffic comes only from its own cluster gets a ferrous routing score: edges to it are deprioritized and its messages expire. To pass, an attacker must seed each fake identity with real, diverse inbound carriers over time, paying bandwidth and latency per identity. Honest nodes leave a broad echo across many carriers, so cloning them is expensive.
